palette.notes: Each 16x16 character uses 3 colours plus an outline (stated in the article); enemy variants are cheap colour swaps; red-tint and inverted frames are used for damage.

lighting: Not covered; flat NES-style shading inside the 3-colour budget.
silhouette: 16x16 characters on a 16x16 tile grid, outlined so they separate from the ground; slimes use one down-facing sprite for all directions.

motion.timing: Most actions use 2 frames; idle and walk reuse the same 2 frames at different speeds. Attack: strike, follow-through and overshoot at 0.08 s each, then 0.32 s before the next attack (stated in the article).
principles: timing changes instead of new drawings

texture: Top-down tiles of grass, sand and water modelled on 8-bit Zelda, Pokemon and Final Fantasy; effects are tiny overlays (X strike spark, 3-frame puff, 2-frame blast).
camera: Top-down, tile-based; no camera moves discussed.

acting.enters: Not covered beyond area design: enemies that fit the setting so each newcomer is memorable.
acting.acts: Reactions do the acting: a hit alternates a red-tinted pain pose with an inverted one; strikes flash an X with a blank frame between.
acting.exits: Enemies vanish with a 3-frame circular puff overlaid while they flash away.
acting.depth: Flat top-down plane; staging is by themed areas rather than depth.

techniques: reuse the same 2 frames for idle and walk at different timing
0.08 s strike/follow-through/overshoot, then a 0.32 s pause
damage flash alternating red-tint and inverted frames
X-shaped strike spark with an empty frame between for a flash
feel: 3 colours + outline + 2-frame actions + loud hit flashes = instantly readable at tiny sizes
for_fred: Give Fred a quick exit: flash, a 3-frame puff, gone; then pop him back somewhere else in the frame later. Reuse his 2-frame idle at a faster rate for excitement instead of drawing new loops.
